description: Spanish glossary of the game's own text (docs/modding/translation-handbook.md). terms: English term of glossary_en.json -> the Spanish form used in every file. keep_latin: unused for a Latin-script language. style: the rules of voice and form. Neutral Spanish, meant to read naturally in Spain and in Latin America.

style.address: Harry and Cybil: tu, both ways. Harry and Lisa: tu, both ways. Harry and Kaufmann: usted, both ways. Dahlia to everyone: tu, elevated and solemn, no colloquial words. Harry to Dahlia: usted until the last scene, tu in the last scene. Dahlia and Kaufmann: tu, both ways. Alessa to Dahlia: mama / mami; Cheryl to Harry: papa. A plural 'you' is always ustedes (the UFO ending, Kaufmann's taunt), never vosotros.
style.neutral: Words that split the regions are avoided where a common one exists: tomar/llevarse instead of coger, accionar instead of pulsar, apretar el boton, encendedor, refrigerador, ascensor, coche, casillero. The past is the simple past (que le hiciste) or the present for system messages; the perfect only for an experience (has visto).
style.gender: First-person lines carry the speaker's gender only in adjectives and participles (sola, segura, descuidada, preocupado): see the list of scenes in translation-handbook.md. Where the speaker is uncertain the line is worded without gender (map6_s01: 'Temia por ti').
style.quotes: “ ” for the [ ] of the English; the dash is the character — (U+2014), which the English writes as '='. Questions and exclamations open with ¿ and ¡.
style.item_in_sentence: an item name inside a sentence is lower case, with its article outside the colour span and the pronoun agreeing with it: 'Hay un <name>. ¿Te lo llevas?' / 'Hay una <name>. ¿Te la llevas?', 'Usas el/la <name>.', 'Consigues un/una <name>.' The span equals the inventory name apart from the capital letter.
style.system_messages: Prompts and results address the player in the second person singular of the present (Usas, Viertes, Deslizas, ¿Quieres...?); Harry's own remarks stay in the first person.
